ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: Poet of the Canzoniere, whose search for classical manuscripts made him a founder of Renaissance humanism.
A republic of bankers and wool merchants whose gold florin became a standard coin of European trade, and the birthplace of the Renaissance.
From 1397 this Byzantine scholar taught Greek in Florence, opening classical Greek literature to the Italian humanists.
His dome for Florence Cathedral, built without wooden centring, is still the largest masonry dome in the world; he is also credited with the first demonstration of linear perspective.
Florence's effective ruler from 1469: poet, diplomat and patron of Botticelli and the young Michelangelo.
Painter of the Last Supper and the Mona Lisa, whose notebooks studied anatomy, mechanics and nature.
Botticelli and Perugino painted its walls; Michelangelo painted its ceiling between 1508 and 1512 and, later, the Last Judgement.
Machiavelli's treatise of 1513 on how new princes win and hold power, written after the Medici's return had cost him his office.
The most famous scholar of the Northern Renaissance, whose Greek New Testament of 1516 and Praise of Folly made him a voice for reform.
